title: SCALA SYNTH -- 16-voice additive synth with Scala (.scl) microtuning

sections.heading: USING IT
lines: Turn on audio with the DSP ON/OFF speaker, then play the KEYBOARD or a MIDI keyboard.
TEST NOTE: ON starts a middle C, OFF releases it.
Load .scl: click the button or drop a .scl file on the box next to it.
Scale / Degrees show the loaded tuning. It starts in 12-TET until a file is loaded.
PARTIALS: how many sine partials each voice uses (1-32).
TILT: how fast upper partials fade. 0 = flat, higher = darker.
STRETCH: partial spacing. 1 = harmonic, above or below 1 = inharmonic, bell-like.
EVEN/ODD: balance between even and odd partials.
DRIFT: slow random detuning of each partial for a moving, organic sound.
ATTACK / DECAY / SUSTAIN / RELEASE: the amplitude envelope of each note.
VOLUME: master level (0-1), shown on the meters.
Partial Amplitudes: the level of each partial. TILT and EVEN/ODD redraw it.
You can also draw on it by hand to shape the spectrum.
Spectrum: live spectrum of the output.

sections.heading: HOW IT WORKS
lines: scala-parser.js reads the .scl file and fills a 128-note frequency table (buffer~ scala-tuning).
poly~ runs 16 voices. Each voice looks up its note's frequency in that table.
A gen~ codebox in each voice sums up to 32 sines, with levels read from the partial-amps buffer.
Each voice has its own adsr~ envelope. Voices are mixed and scaled by VOLUME.
